phase_name: Permission Broker Production Consumption Operational Hardening
summary: Bounded production operational hardening closing both findings 148G carried forward from 148F. F-148F-3 (PBPC-001 v1.2 Section 17, PBPC-REQ-059-061 final pre-dispatch re-observation, prior status REPAIR_REQUIRED_BEFORE_CLOSURE): independently re-derived the requirement -- re-observe local HEAD, branch, unpushed-commit count, and active task ID (the four fields PBPC-REQ-056 identifies as locally, transactionally bindable) immediately before each of pcae push's two dispatch sites; any mismatch against the value bound at broker-evaluation time is material (PBPC-REQ-060); material mismatch invalidates the existing ALLOW, dispatches nothing, and requires a fresh evaluation cycle, not an automatic in-place re-evaluation (PBPC-REQ-061). Implemented via a new in-process _PushDecisionSnapshot (head, branch, unpushed, task_id; never persisted) captured inside _evaluate_push_permission at the moment of broker evaluation, and a new shared _validate_push_permission_freshness() helper called immediately before each real git push dispatch on both the ordinary (run_push) and --staged-file-aware (_run_push_staged_file_aware) paths. CLOSED. F-148F-1 (PermissionBroker() construction outside its adapter's try/except, prior status REPAIR_RECOMMENDED_POST_CLOSURE): widened _evaluate_push_permission's existing try: block to cover PermissionBroker() construction as well as .evaluate(), following the established local precedent (command_path_observation.py:70-84, which already wraps construction and evaluation together for its own broker touchpoint). Construction failure now produces the same graceful 'Push blocked: Permission Broker evaluation failed (...)' diagnostic and exit code 1 that evaluation failure already produced, instead of an uncaught exception. CLOSED. Test hygiene: repaired the stale 148C.10-era invariant test (test_push_module_does_not_import_permission_broker, latent since 148E's intentional PermissionBroker wiring, identified as REPOSITORY_TEST_HYGIENE_DEBT by 148G) -- renamed/rewritten to test_push_module_is_the_authorized_pbpc_production_consumer, asserting push.py IS the authorized production consumer while pcae.commands.agent and pcae.commands.phase (148F/148G's independently inventoried unrelated dispatch sites) remain unwired. Rewrote two 148F tests (test_ordinary_path_broker_construction_failure_does_not_dispatch, test_staged_file_aware_broker_construction_failure_does_not_dispatch) that had encoded the pre-repair F-148F-1 bug as expected behavior (pytest.raises(RuntimeError, ...) around main([...])) -- both docstrings explicitly predicted this exact rewrite once repaired. Added tests/test_permission_broker_push_operational_hardening.py (9 new tests): validation ordering (source-level assertion that broker evaluation < final re-observation < dispatch, both paths); no-drift control (ordinary path dispatches exactly once); HEAD drift (ordinary + staged paths); branch drift; task-ID drift (no fabricated replacement ID); multiple simultaneous drift; genuine (non-forged) broker ALLOW still blocked by drift (the central F-148F-3 closure proof, using a real PermissionBrokerDecision instance, not a duck-typed fake); stale-ALLOW-cannot-be-reused-but-a-fresh-rerun-succeeds (proves PBPC-REQ-061's 'fresh evaluation cycle required', evaluate() called again on the second attempt). Regression: tests/test_permission_broker_push_production_consumption.py + tests/test_phase_148f_permission_broker_production_consumption_independent_verification.py 31/31 passed (2 rewritten); tests/test_phase_148c10_pbpc_v12_independent_verification.py 20/20 passed (1 rewritten); new tests/test_permission_broker_push_operational_hardening.py 9/9 passed; tests/test_permission_broker.py + test_permission_broker_foundation.py + test_permission_broker_policy_applicability.py + test_phase_148c7_permission_broker_policy_applicability_independent_verification.py + test_phase_148c8_permission_broker_production_consumption_b1_reevaluation.py 455/455 passed (no PBPA/Foundation drift); tests/test_runtime_inspect_cli.py + test_runtime_snapshot.py + test_runtime_context.py 186/186 passed (runtime unchanged, no coupling); full push-suite regression (test_push.py, test_staged_file_aware_push.py, test_commit_push_gate.py, test_push_phase_report_identity_137f1.py, test_post_push_canonicalization.py, test_push_state_reconciliation.py, test_commit_push_preflight.py, test_commit_push_preflight_review.py) 186/186 passed; Fast Green (python -m pytest -m fast_green -n auto -q) 4391 passed, unchanged from the 148D/E/F/G baseline. Production diff: exactly one src/pcae/** file changed (src/pcae/commands/push.py), matching this phase's budget; git diff --name-only <pre-148G.1>..HEAD -- docs/contracts/ empty (PBPC-001 remains v1.2, PBPA-001 remains v1.0, both unamended); git diff --name-only <pre-148G.1>..HEAD -- src/pcae/core/permission_broker_foundation.py src/pcae/core/permission_broker.py empty (no policy semantics changed); HARD_BLOCK_REGISTRY independently recounted: 12 entries, unchanged. Deliberate deviation: 148G's own recommendation text additionally suggested adding a 'construction failure' row to PBPC-001 Section 18's failure-ownership table -- the actual 148G.1 governing task instructions explicitly prohibit amending PBPC-001, so this specific sub-item was not done; flagged rather than silently dropped, left as an open item for a future, separately-scoped contract-amendment phase. Runtime reconfirmed Observed/observe/unavailable; IWC/AESIC/Runtime Enforcement independence reconfirmed unchanged; Prompt Generation (Phase 45F) remains DEFERRED, untouched. See docs/PHASE_148G.1_PERMISSION_BROKER_PRODUCTION_CONSUMPTION_OPERATIONAL_HARDENING.md for full detail.
tests_added_or_updated: tests/test_permission_broker_push_operational_hardening.py (new, 9 tests); tests/test_phase_148f_permission_broker_production_consumption_independent_verification.py (2 tests rewritten to assert repaired F-148F-1 behavior); tests/test_phase_148c10_pbpc_v12_independent_verification.py (1 test renamed/rewritten to assert the current, correct PBPC production-consumer invariant). Regression re-run: 31/31 (148E/148F PBPC suites) + 20/20 (148C.10 suite) + 9/9 (new hardening suite) + 455/455 (Foundation/PBPA) + 186/186 (runtime) + 186/186 (push-suite regression, 8 files) + Fast Green 4391/4391, all passed.
